items.title: 56706_Buddy Tate oral history interview
items.q: This is after he'd fired Prez and Don was in the band and Don was really almost an alcoholic at that time.

ctx.x: You know what I mean? It was like a little dungeon into -- that's where we used to work at night. You'd come right up and you'd come right into the Hotel Edison. Well, she had all the big bands there, Miss Kramer. They were called the Blue Room. Artie Shaw, Harry James, Benny and everybody played there for Mrs. Maria Kramer, was her name. But now you could go down under there, then across the street, there was a bar by the name of Martin's and they used to sell

three for one, one price, they'd sell three drinks. So Basie didn't know this bar was under there, you know, he didn't know what was going on down in this tunnel. So, you know, he would look up sometime and cats would be high on the bandstand and everything. So I know he would have a valet to go in their cases and their overcoats and things and -- but they couldn't find anything. So I knew what was going on. Then I didn't drink a drop. I would just go to work. But I'd go over there, because we had a lot of fun,…

But Don used to say to me, we were friendly, he says, "Look, Buddy," he says, "I know you're a friend of mine and I know you admire me and I admire you. Now look at it this way. If I'm really goofing and messing up, I'll take your advice, when you tell me I'm really goofing," he says, "I'll listen to you, because you're sober. You've got to see what's going on." So I said, "Well, that's very nice." And he really did that, until this night when he drew that gun on everybody.
